note: The single source of truth for what is measured and how it is built.
Nothing in tests/bench/ may hard-code a version, a compiler flag, or a
physical constant: it is read from here, or generated from here.
Written before anything was built, because a benchmark that cannot name
the commit it measured cannot be disputed -- which is how the paper came
to record three codes as version '2026-08', the month they were cloned.

Versions were verified to be the latest OFFICIAL releases on 2026-08-07, not merely the ones the paper happened to use: full tag lists, the two download pages, and a diff of each NuFast tag against its branch HEAD.

Each code's `timing_scripts` names the script that produces its numbers today. These are the drivers the new pipeline replaces with adapters under tests/bench/adapters/; one of them, the NuFast-LBL accuracy driver, is recorded as MISSING because it was never committed.

AMORTIZED.definition: Timed region is a scan of `scan.steps` steps, each step = configure(one varying parameter) + evaluate(whole grid). Everything invariant under that scan is hoisted outside: body/Earth object, engine construction, profile installation, grid arrays, all other setters.
AMORTIZED.normalization: microseconds per grid point = total / (steps * n_points)
AMORTIZED.claim: cost inside a fit or scan, with each code's caching working as designed
AMORTIZED.rationale: Adopted from the NuFast-Earth author's own harness, src/examples/Speed.cpp::Atmospheric_Speed, so the definition is his rather than ours.

THROUGHPUT.definition: Timed region is one request for N points. Codes that batch get one call; codes that cannot get a loop in their own language inside evaluate(), labelled as a loop.
THROUGHPUT.normalization: microseconds per point, as a curve in N
THROUGHPUT.claim: what batching buys, and which interfaces expose it

_dropped.ONESHOT: Dropped by decision. It excluded JIT and import by fiat, so it was never language-fair, and it is the protocol whose numbers started the dispute. The oneshot/amortized ratio it was to provide is not published.

protocols.no_crossing_rule: Every artifact record carries a protocol stamp {name, grid} and a conventions stamp, now 'own-reference' for the per-code references. The figure builders assert all series on one axes share both stamps, and the paper-number test refuses to bind a macro comparing two numbers with different stamps. Series differenced against per-code references may share an axes -- that is the point -- but may not be mixed with any series differenced against a shared reference.

ACCURACY.definition: Untimed. Configure once, ask for the probabilities, difference them against a 50-digit reference built in THIS CODE'S OWN convention. No clock is read, so an accuracy number can never be mistaken for a speed.
ACCURACY.normalization: max absolute deviation over the grid
ACCURACY.claim: how accurate this code's algorithm is on the problem it was actually handed

OSC/100x100.why: NuFast-Earth caches across zenith angles; a 12x1 grid hides an ~8x per-probability advantage it shows here. Objection Earth-3.

speed.policy: Each code is built with ITS OWN upstream flags, so we never publish a code slower than its authors do.

accuracy.policy: Every code built -O3 -std=c++17, no -Ofast and no -ffast-math, because value-changing flags make an accuracy axis measure the flag.

build_profiles.why_two: One flag set cannot serve both axes. The previous setup used -Ofast -ffast-math for one dataset and -O3 for another and presented them as one methodology.

thread_policy.definition: Each code runs with the parallelism it naturally uses; no code is forced to one thread. The effective thread count is captured per code per run and recorded in the artifact.
thread_policy.why: Forcing OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 would strip this library's prange kernels (16 of them) while leaving other codes' advantages intact -- not neutral, and it would silently move our own published figures.
thread_policy.requirement: Any cross-code speed claim must quote the thread counts of both codes.

precision_knobs.rtol: 1e-3..1e-5, which is where it actually stops: on CHORD/12x1 the slab product's error estimate bottoms out near 7e-8 at the 1024-slab ceiling, so a tighter rtol raises rather than returns. Was advertised as 1e-3..1e-15; ten of those settings crash. The small residuals are reached through n_slabs_per_segment instead.

note: Measured, at last.  The manifest previously asserted this code
floors at 3e-3 'because of its constants'.  That was an inherited
claim about an intrinsic defect that nobody had tested, and it is
wrong by seven orders.  Swept at three flavors, E=10 GeV,
cosz=-0.9, against nuCraft's own 50-digit reference, the error
tracks numPrec the whole way down and is still falling by 3x at
the edge of the declared domain: there is no floor above 7.9e-11.
That is exactly what zvode at atol=rtol=numPrec*2e-3 predicts and
nothing else.  Asserting a floor for a dial we never turned is the
failure this pipeline exists to prevent, and it was aimed at
another author's code.

note: The one set of mixing parameters every code is handed. NuFit values,
as the paper's appendix specifies. No adapter may contain a literal
for any of these; conversions.h carries them into C++ and runner.py
into Python, so 'the same values for all codes' is structural rather
than a thing to remember.
Where a code wants a different PARAMETERISATION of the same physics
-- Prob3++ takes Dmsq32, nuCraft takes angles rather than sin^2 --
the conversion is derived in conversions.py, never re-typed.
The 3+1 point of the paper's sterile oscillogram, the same one
tests/prem_scan.py uses, so the benchmark and the paper's figure
describe one physics point rather than two.  Needed because the
CHORD/12x1 grid carries energies_gev_3plus1 and the nuCraft
never_absorbed exception bites only at four flavors -- neither
could be run while these were absent.
theta34 = 0 exactly, so no angle is invented for it.
One 50-digit reference PER CODE, each built with that code's own hbar c
and its own matter normalisation, and with the SAME mixing parameters as
every other. Each code is handed honest physical inputs and differenced
against the problem it actually solves, so the residual measures its
algorithm rather than a unit convention.
This replaces rescaling each code's density and baseline to reproduce our
potential, which made our own code the only one receiving an
apples-to-apples problem -- part of what was objected to. The mass-defect
factors therefore move from being fudges applied to codes into inputs of
the reference builder; adapters no longer carry them at all.
PLOTTING: all codes still go on ONE axes, with |P - P_ref| on y, exactly as
before -- what changes is that P_ref is now each code's own reference. The
quantity is per-code but it is the same KIND of quantity for every series,
which is what makes them comparable: how well does each code solve the
problem it was handed. Every caption must say that P_ref differs per code.
A CONSEQUENCE WORTH NOTING: no figure's floor is a convention artifact any
more. The old six-ways comparison was capped near 1e-8 by a deliberate
4.2e-8 hbar-c mismatch, which is the floor that prompted the objection that
our accuracy comparison was not apples-to-apples. That cap is gone, so that
figure's framing -- 'what a convention mismatch costs' -- is now a sentence
rather than a figure, and every code can reach round-off if it can.

never_absorbed.nuCraft: Its charged-current and sterile entries are 15.256e-5 and 7.6525e-5. nuCraft's own derivation (NuCraft.py:205-212) defines ONE prefactor for the vector (2Ye,0,0,1-Ye), so by its own formula the two must be exactly 2:1. 15.256e-5 is exactly twice that prefactor for m = 931.5 MeV, the amu; 7.6525e-5 would need m = 928.5 MeV, which is not the amu, the proton, the neutron, or the 0.939 its own comment states. The pair is therefore inconsistent with its own documented derivation rather than expressing a different convention, most likely a digit typo for 7.6325e-5 (half the modern 7.63247e-5) -- the same defect class as its rICore = 1121.5 for 1221.5. Its reference uses its constants for the units and the exact isoscalar ratio. NOTE this bites ONLY at 3+1: at three flavors the sterile entries do not exist, so no three-flavor figure is affected by this exception either way.

plotting.caption_must_state: that P_ref is built in each code's own convention, with shared mixing parameters

note: CONTINUOUS for every code. There is one physical Earth -- the continuous
PREM -- and every code is scored by how far its answer sits from it.
Codes approximate that Earth differently, and the approximation is part of
what is being measured rather than something a reference should forgive.
Prob3++ and GLoBES cannot express anything but constant layers: their
interfaces take (radius, rho) rows and (length, density) pairs. Their
discretisation is therefore intrinsic to using them, it is real error a
user pays, and it is swept via n_shells so the convergence is visible.
nuSQuIDS (Akima), nuCraft (linear spline) and this library (PREM
polynomial) all see a density that varies inside each interval.
NuFast-Earth is given a continuous profile too, on OUR PREM with the
shared Ye = 0.5, via constant_shells = false. NOT its own PREM_Full:
that polynomial is identical to ours, but PREM_Full_Ye returns 0.466
below 3480 km and 0.494 above, where every other code gets 0.5 -- it
would have handed one code a different matter potential.
MEASURED, and this is why the earlier as-handed basis was abandoned:
scoring the compiled codes against the shell stack we handed them put
Prob3++ and GLoBES at 1e-13 while this library sat at 4e-7. Against the
continuous PREM all three land at 4.06e-7 -- the same number, because it
is the discretisation and not the code. The as-handed basis was
symmetric but empty: every series flat at round-off, measuring solver
self-consistency rather than distance from the Earth.
profile_basis.rule: Every accuracy artifact is differenced against the continuous PREM in that code's own hbar c and matter normalisation. The discretisation each code uses is swept where the code exposes it, and stated per series in the caption.

two_configurations.NuFast-Earth: ACCURACY uses constant_shells = false, so the engine integrates the continuous profile. That defeats its eigenvalue caching -- eigens_varying, one decomposition per (energy, cosz, layer). SPEED must use the stepped configuration, which is where its zenith caching and the Earth-3 advantage live. The two configurations may never share an axes.

artifact_requirements.threads: Every series must record the thread count the code actually used, not the policy. A cross-code speed claim without both counts is not a claim.
artifact_requirements.kernel_entered: For NuOscProbExact, record which compiled kernel was entered (probabilities_3nu_kernel for constant density, earth_chords_3nu_kernel for a chord). Nothing currently asserts this at run time, so a missing numba would have us publish the NumPy path as ours.
artifact_requirements.statistics: {mean, sd, min, n}; the schema has no field for a bare scalar time.
artifact_requirements.stamps: protocol {name, grid} and conventions; series with different stamps may not share an axes.
artifact_requirements.machine: cpu, cores, governor, load average, and the session's three canary readings.

scored_channel.note: bench.hpp says probabilities() appends 'the scored channel' and never said which. Every adapter's checksum already sums numu->numu (m[1][1], GetProb(2,2), _PMM=4, EvalFlavor(1)), so that is the channel, recorded here before the accuracy path is written. Note CONST/N-sweep's grid entry says numu->nue for the THROUGHPUT figure's problem statement; the scored channel for accuracy is numu->numu. A wrong guess here silently changes every accuracy figure.
